question: Did any prospects raise HIPAA or BAA requirements?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract every statement where the prospect or OrbitFlow staff raises HIPAA, a BAA (business associate agreement), or healthcare data privacy/protected health information requirements, including whether OrbitFlow confirmed, denied, or hedged on meeting them.
assumptions: Question asks about prospect calls only, so call_types is restricted to Prospect.
Company names not mentioned, so companies is empty.
BrightPath Health is the most likely healthcare prospect but was not named, so no company filter is applied.

findings.speaker: Tom Alvarez
findings.quote: We're not healthcare.
findings.context: Tom Alvarez stated Acme Logistics is not a healthcare company, which bears on whether HIPAA or healthcare privacy requirements apply. — Said while listing the security review requirements; he did not name HIPAA or a BAA, and he did not ask OrbitFlow for one.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Baseline is SOC 2 Type II. SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise.
findings.context: OrbitFlow's security baseline (SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SAML, encryption, audit logs, EU residency on Enterprise) was described without any mention of HIPAA or a BAA. — Jon Bell's security answer; no HIPAA or BAA confirmation, denial, or hedge was given.

findings.speaker: Tom Alvarez
findings.quote: We need the usual vendor review, SSO, audit logs. We don't have a special data-residency requirement for this project.
findings.context: No HIPAA or BAA requirement appears to have been raised by the prospect on this call; the security list was described as shorter than most, with no healthcare gate. — Inferred from the absence of any HIPAA or BAA request in the security discussion and from the prospect saying the gating issue was not security.

findings.speaker: Elliot Greene
findings.quote: The BAA is the gate. If you can't offer one, we cannot use OrbitFlow for any workflow that may involve protected health information.
findings.context: Elliot Greene says the BAA is a hard gate: without one, OrbitFlow cannot be used for any workflow that may involve PHI. — Stated as the first gate on the security list, before any other evaluation.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: I'm not going to give you a yes on this call. What I will do is get you a written answer from our legal and compliance side within
findings.context: Maya Chen declines to confirm BAA support on the call and commits to a written answer from legal and compliance within about a week. — Hedge, not a yes or no. Jon Bell confirms the one-week timeline for a written position.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: A week is realistic for a written position, yes.
findings.context: Jon Bell says a written position on the BAA is realistic within one week. — Confirms the timeline Maya proposed.

findings.speaker: Elliot Greene
findings.quote: A written position is fine. A verbal "we're working on it" is not.
findings.context: Elliot Greene requires a written BAA position, not a verbal assurance. — Sets the standard for how the BAA question must be answered.

findings.speaker: Elliot Greene
findings.quote: Policy says it shouldn't. In practice we do occasionally find patient names in free-text fields.
findings.context: Elliot Greene says BrightPath sometimes has patient names in HubSpot free-text fields, despite policy saying patient information should not go there. — Correction of his earlier statement. It is a PHI control gap, and he wants the design to account for the actual data, not the policy version.

findings.speaker: Priya Shah
findings.quote: compliance review slows down any workflow that touches patient-adjacent data, which is most of them.
findings.context: Priya Shah says most of BrightPath's workflows touch patient-adjacent data, so compliance review slows them down. — Describes the current-state compliance bottleneck behind the backlog.

findings.speaker: Priya Shah
findings.quote: Procurement will not have a serious pricing conversation until security tells us whether the BAA requirement can be met.
findings.context: Priya Shah says procurement will not discuss pricing until security confirms whether the BAA requirement can be met, and privacy counsel reviews the DPA and BAA. — The BAA gates commercial discussions and is a separate approval gate with privacy counsel.

findings.speaker: Priya Shah
findings.quote: My read is I would still consider a limited pilot with synthetic or clearly non-PHI data.
findings.context: Priya Shah is open to a limited pilot only with synthetic or clearly non-PHI data, pending the BAA answer. — Pilot scope is constrained by the PHI question. Maya Chen commits to sending the written BAA position within a week.

findings.speaker: Sophie Reed
findings.quote: We need a standard DPA. SSO would be nice rather than mandatory
findings.context: Sophie Reed asked for a standard DPA and said SSO would be nice rather than mandatory; she framed security needs around UK/EU customer data, not healthcare or HIPAA. — Security/compliance discussion; no HIPAA, BAA, or PHI mentioned. Included because compliance requirements were raised, though not healthcare-specific.

findings.speaker: Sophie Reed
findings.quote: because we sell into the UK and EU I want to understand where customer data actually gets processed.
findings.context: Sophie Reed said they sell into UK and EU and wants to understand where customer data gets processed. — Data residency concern raised as a security/compliance point; no mention of HIPAA, BAA, or protected health information.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: EU data residency is available on Enterprise. On Growth, I'd need to confirm the default processing region for you in writing rather than guess.
findings.context: OrbitFlow said EU data residency is available on Enterprise only; on Growth it would need to confirm the default processing region in writing rather than guess. — Vendor hedged on the data-processing location question for the Growth tier; no HIPAA or BAA statement made.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: I'll also get you written answers on the Shopify trigger coverage and the default processing region.
findings.context: OrbitFlow committed to sending written answers on the default processing region, which Leo said he had dodged. — Follow-up action on data processing location; HIPAA/BAA not addressed.

findings.speaker: Hannah Cole
findings.quote: If you can't satisfy those, connector breadth will not save the project.
findings.context: HIPAA and BAA are not raised in this call; the prospect's compliance gates are model risk and auditability, with no healthcare data or PHI requirement mentioned. — Ember Financial is a financial services firm; the call discusses compliance (SOC 2, model risk, audit), but no HIPAA, BAA, or protected health information requirement appears. The only related term is generic 'compliance' in the sense of model governance, not healthcare.

findings.speaker: Ben Foster
findings.quote: normal GDPR terms, and — this one matters — written reassurance that our client documents aren't used to train models.
findings.context: Prospect raised general data-privacy and compliance requirements (GDPR, no training on client documents) but did not mention HIPAA, a BAA, or protected health information. — Closest related topic is security/GDPR and client-document confidentiality for an agency, not healthcare data. Included because the question asks about compliance requirements; no HIPAA or BAA was raised in this call.

findings.speaker: Alastair McCrae
findings.quote: we're fully GDPR compliant, so that's all covered.
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff said the platform is fully GDPR compliant and that it does not train on customer data, and agreed to send a DPA. No HIPAA or BAA claim was made. — Vendor response to the privacy requirement; this is GDPR/DPA territory, not HIPAA or BAA.

findings.speaker: Ava Sinclair
findings.quote: Regional controls. What does that mean concretely?
findings.context: Customer's security list includes regional controls, which Ava links to EU data residency; no HIPAA or BAA is raised. — Compliance-adjacent requirement only; HIPAA/BAA/PHI are not mentioned anywhere in this call, so the closest topic is general data residency, not healthcare privacy.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: SOC 2 Type II is the baseline.
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff listed its security and compliance baseline: SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO/SCIM, encryption, audit logs. No HIPAA or BAA was offered or discussed. — Vendor compliance statement with no healthcare-specific commitment; the absence of HIPAA/BAA is itself notable for the question asked.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: EU data residency is available on Enterprise.
findings.context: OrbitFlow confirmed EU data residency on Enterprise, but did not address healthcare data or protected health information. — Residency is the only regional privacy commitment discussed; it is not a HIPAA answer.

findings.speaker: Marcus Chen
findings.quote: It's in two contracts. Both enterprise accounts.
findings.context: Customer says EU residency commitments exist in two enterprise contracts, and is checking whether there are more. — Contractual data-privacy commitments, not HIPAA or BAA; the customer's own compliance obligations are not described as healthcare.

draft.answer: Yes, one prospect did: BrightPath Health made a BAA a hard gate for any workflow that may involve PHI [C1]. OrbitFlow's Maya Chen would not confirm BAA support on the call and promised a written answer within about a week, which Jon Bell said was realistic [C2]. BrightPath also said procurement will not discuss pricing until the BAA question is resolved, and it would consider only a limited pilot with non-PHI data [C3]. No other prospect raised HIPAA or a BAA [C4].

claims.text: BrightPath Health's Security Architect Elliot Greene said the BAA is the gate: without one, OrbitFlow cannot be used for any workflow that may involve protected health information. He also said a written BAA position is required, and a verbal 'we're working on it' is not acceptable.

Maya Chen (Account Executive) declined to give a yes on BAA support during the call and committed to a written answer from legal and compliance within about a week. Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer) confirmed a week is realistic for a written position.

Priya Shah (Head of Business Systems) said procurement will not have a serious pricing conversation until security confirms whether the BAA requirement can be met, and that privacy counsel reviews the DPA and BAA. She said most BrightPath workflows touch patient-adjacent data, and she would still consider a limited pilot with synthetic or clearly non-PHI data. Elliot Greene added that patient names occasionally turn up in HubSpot free-text fields despite policy, so the design should account for the actual data.

No HIPAA or BAA requirement was raised in the other prospect calls. Acme Logistics said 'We're not healthcare' and OrbitFlow's security answer there did not mention HIPAA. Cedar & Finch, Fable Media and Juniper Cloud Tools raised only DPA, GDPR or EU data residency topics. Ember Financial's compliance gates were model risk and auditability, which appears not to involve HIPAA. OrbitFlow's vendor responses on those calls did not offer HIPAA or BAA commitments.

not_covered: Whether OrbitFlow's written BAA position was ever delivered, and what it said.
The other 4 of the 10 prospect calls read had no relevant findings.
